correctness.rationale: For every admissible joint law a one-edge normalized adversarial matrix gives exactly four times the probability the derived vertex signing fails to cut that edge, providing a lower bound valid for nonlinear or Z-dependent couplings. Independently mixing uniform signs with an optimal fractional-cover cut distribution yields two individually uniform probes and a diagonal covariance of all edge sign monomials, attaining this lower bound for every graph. The two-way scaling equivalence with the finite fractional-cut-cover LP is exact; bipartiteness, edge transitivity, clique parities, odd cycles and the pendant-triangle counterexample follow from explicit finite combinatorics. Offdiagonal energy counts unordered edges. The extracted standalone script passed 594 finite LP/covariance/combinatorial checks; no infinite generality rests on numerical sampling.

originality.rationale: The graph fractional-cut-cover LP and standard Rademacher variance formula are expressly credited as prior. The examined full-text fixed-matrix nonlinear coupling results optimize a different quantifier order, and existing partition-based stochastic probing does not cover arbitrary couplings of two full-cube-uniform marginals. A matching all-couplings robust lower bound and an optimal graph-only mixed-cut law for every sparsity graph were not found in the inspected scientific statements; dyadic complete-graph constants are already partly attained by known Hadamard constructions and are not singled out as novel. This remains provisional historical priority, not a uniqueness certification.
residual_risks: The full Neto–Ben-Ameur 2019 article was not available; only publisher/institution metadata and abstract were read, so potential specialist graph-theoretic implications are not ruled out.
The 2023 weighted-cut-cover paper was read in relevant introductory portions but not all 38 pages; the parameter is deliberately credited as known.
Related trace-estimation literature may have an equivalent matrix-blind all-couplings minimax theorem under different terminology; lack of a matching search result is not proof of originality.
A previously developed shared-sign Hadamard construction already realizes certain dyadic complete-graph values; no novel credit is assigned to those numbers.
Independent historical-priority and mathematical audit are not performed.

value.rationale: For unknown coefficients with known sparsity, two full sign probes consume the minimum nontrivial query budget beyond one baseline; the theorem solves the exact worst-case variance design over arbitrary dependence, not merely a fixed-stencil or known-weight example. It connects robust numerical estimation to an established fractional cut-cover invariant, constructs a matching optimal law, proves zero robust variance iff the graph is bipartite and a factor-at-least-two separation from all deterministic flips on every nonbipartite graph, and demonstrates the essential distinction between graph-robust and matrix-specific nonlinear couplings. These are motivated, sharp structural boundaries with immediate interpretation for sensor/probe allocation, not new notation for a known count. The result does not promise efficient construction or downstream algorithms in all graph sizes.
